name: Balinese Malay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Balinese Malay: only survey/classification refs (McDowell & Anderbeck 2020, Asmah 1985, Adelaar & Prentice 1996); no phonological description found

sources.citation: Garuda (garuda.kemdiktisaintek.go.id) search 'Melayu Loloan' (9 hits) and Crossref/DOAJ/Neliti searches, 2026-09-17
sources.note: Only the two Suparwa Linguistika articles and Putra et al. 2015 are phonological; the rest are sociolinguistic/pragmatic (Suparwa 2008 Bumi Lestari 'Ekologi Bahasa'; Fahmi et al. 2016 imperative politeness; Suparwa & Satyawati 2019 narrative discourse; Suparwa et al. 2020 ritual language; Sosiowati et al. 2025 Burdah/Ngelenggang) and were not opened.

sources.citation: Kurniawan, Muh. Ardian. 2015 [OSF preprint 2017]. Inovasi Fonologis dalam Bahasa Melayu Loloan: Kajian Dialektologi Diakronis. In Satyawati et al. (eds), Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar on Austronesian-Non Austronesian Languages and Literature, Udayana University, 350-356. Denpasar: Pustaka Larasan. doi:10.31227/osf.io/vtr7k
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (image-only scan, scanned to.). Diachronic segmental reflexes of Proto-Malayic only; 'penultima' appears only as a position label for vowel changes.

sources.citation: Putra, Anak Agung Putu; Ni Luh Nyoman Seri Malini & I Nyoman Suparwa. 2015. Adaptasi Kosakata Bahasa Bali dalam Bahasa Melayu Loloan Bali. LITERA 14(1): 1-11. doi:10.21831/ltr.v14i1.4404
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives the six-vowel phoneme inventory /i e u o ə a/ with lax allophones after Suparwa 2007 and segmental adaptation of Balinese loans; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Paauw, Scott. 2008. The Malay contact varieties of eastern Indonesia: a typological comparison. PhD, SUNY Buffalo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Loloan; only lists Loloan Malay (p. 22) as a West-Indonesian Malay variety with a note that Sumarsono 1993 gives very limited linguistic information.

sources.citation: Suparwa, I Nyoman. 2008. Persoalan Ortografi untuk Bunyi Hambat-Glotal dalam Bahasa Melayu Loloan Bali. Linguistika 15(29), September 2008: 181-194.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement; 'tekanan' occurs once (p. 192) only in saying the apostrophe is a suprasegmental symbol used e.g. for stress marking. Describes syllable structure (onset-rime-nucleus-coda) and glottal-stop allophony. Cites the author's dissertation Suparwa 2007 'Pola Bunyi Bahasa Melayu Loloan Bali: Kajian Fonologi Leksikal dan Posleksikal' (Udayana).

sources.citation: Suparwa, I Nyoman. 2007. Fonologi Posleksikal dalam Bahasa Melayu Loloan Bali. Linguistika: Buletin Ilmiah Program Magister Linguistik Universitas Udayana 14(27), September 2007 (33 pp. as downloaded).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Whole article is on postlexical segmental rules (contraction, glide insertion); it says only that postlexical rules in principle cover segmental and 'suprasegmental (prosodik)' change and that intonation should be studied in future work. No 'tekanan' or 'aksen' anywhere.

sources.citation: Djendra, Wajan. 1970. Omong Kampung, Sebuah Deskripsi tentang Dialek Melayu di Bali. MA thesis, Universitas Udayana, Denpasar. iv+140 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Earliest general description of the dialect (Glottolog's top descriptive reference); a 140-page deskripsi would normally include a fonologi chapter with tekanan.

sources.citation: Kurniawan, Muh. Ardian. 2013. Enklave Melayu Loloan di Bali dan Enklave Melayu Ampenan di Lombok: Studi Dialektologi Diakronis. MA thesis, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Dialectological thesis with Swadesh-based field data on Loloan; may contain a synchronic phonology chapter with a stress note.

sources.citation: Suparwa, I Nyoman. 2007. Pola Bunyi Bahasa Melayu Loloan Bali: Kajian Fonologi Leksikal dan Posleksikal. Disertasi, Program Doktor Linguistik, Universitas Udayana, Denpasar.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only full phonology of the language (generative, lexical and postlexical); the derived articles give segment inventory and syllable structure, so the dissertation is where a stress/suprasegmental statement would be if one exists.

sources.citation: Sumarsono. 1993. Pemertahanan Bahasa Melayu Loloan di Bali. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xiii+302 pp. (= PhD Universitas Indonesia 1990, OCLC 769721001)

sources.note: Book-length study of the community; Paauw 2008 says it has very limited linguistic information, but it may include a short structural sketch; also the source most secondary works cite.
